title: Semantic-stability oracle + staged human review for cost-driven batching/cache changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create an automatic quality-regression gating system for batching/caching/quantization recommendations that prioritizes semantic fidelity over raw token-match and integrates a staged human review path before full apply. The system — the 'semantic-stability oracle' — combines embedding-based drift measures, structured-output checks, and lightweight syntactic heuristics to detect regressions that are subtle but user-visible. This ticket designs the evaluation composition, numeric acceptance thresholds per workload class, the canary/rollback decision logic, and the human sampling protocol for spot checks when the oracle is near the decision boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Define an eval suite that covers production prompt distributions, edge-case adversarial prompts, and a representative reference exemplar set
Implement embedding-based similarity metric (cosine on model-agnostic embeddings) and a composite score combining semantic similarity + intent-preservation checks
Establish per-workload numeric thresholds and a two-tier decision rule: auto-apply pass, human-review queue on borderline, block + rollback on fail
Shadow-run framework that collects 10k paired responses and produces a stability report within 24 hours
Human sampling protocol with stratified sampling and annotation rubric implemented in the console
Dashboards and alerts surface regression severity and recommended rollback actions
eval_suite: Production sample: 5k recent prompts stratified by route and model
Long-tail bucket: 1k lower-frequency prompts (rare intents, long contexts)
Adversarial set: 500 prompts designed to trigger hallucinations and entity drift
Reference exemplar set: 200 curated prompts with high-quality reference outputs for intent and entity checks
Structured-output cases: 300 prompts expecting JSON/CSV tables to validate schema preservation
metrics: Semantic cosine (embedding) delta: primary signal; threshold per workload
Intent-preservation score: classifier-based probability that intent label is unchanged
Entity F1 drift: named-entity extraction comparison for critical fields
Syntactic deviation: normalized token edit distance for structured outputs
Latency and token-cost delta: to ensure cost gains are realized and not masked
Human pass-rate: percentage of sampled items accepted by annotators
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Offline analysis: run eval suite on current baseline and proposed config in offline mode; produce stability report
Stage 1 - Shadow canary (0% apply): route live traffic to both configs in shadow and collect 10k paired responses
Stage 2 - Progressive canary (1% -> 5% -> 20%): at each step evaluate metrics; auto-advance only if composite score > pass_threshold
Stage 3 - Human-reviewed canary: if composite score within [border_low, border_high], sample N=200 stratified items for human audit before advancing
Stage 4 - Ramp or rollback: if fail at any step, execute fast rollback and create postmortem; if pass, ramp to 100% with monitoring hooks
human_review_protocol: Sampling: stratified by route, prompt length, and previous failure modes; minimum N=200 for borderline cases
Annotation rubric: preserve intent (binary), entity correctness (critical fields), hallucination flag, and overall quality (1-5)
Acceptance policy: >=90% intent-preservation and <=5% critical-entity-errors to approve without rollback
Escalation: any critical-entity-errors >5% triggers immediate rollback and investigation
Audit trail: all human decisions recorded with annotator ID, timestamps, and example diffs
